name: Матовий майстер: мат на f7
description:
You already know the Scholar’s Mate. Your opponent did not defend very well and you could easily mate his king.

Now, things get a bit harder. What to do if Black tries to prevent the Scholar’s Mate? Then you need real mate monster powers to win the game!

Take a look at the examples to learn how you can still attempt a Scholar’s Mate.

What do you have to do?

Your goal is checkmate on f7 (the red square). Your bishop and queen are going to help each other. Come up with a plan: which moves do you need to play to checkmate the king?

examples.text:
White’s queen and bishop both point at the red square (f7). 
To prevent Scholar’s Mate, Black moves a pawn between f7 and the queen.
This blocks the queen and attacks her at the same time!

The queen needs to get out, but she does so in a canny way…
The queen moves back two squares diagonally, where she threatens mate on f7 once again! 
Black is unaware of this and moves his knight.
White’s queen captures the pawn on f7: checkmate!

Two of White’s pieces are attacking the pawn on f7. However, the pawn is twice guarded as well: by the king and by the knight on the edge.

Fortunately, you know how to deal with protectors: remove them!

So, White’s bishop takes the knight.
If Black does not recapture, White wins 3 points.

And what if Black does take back? Then, the queen moves to f7: checkmate!

examples.pgn: {[%cal Rc4f7]} 1. d6 {[%cal Gd1d5]} Bb6 2. Qd5 {[%csl Rf7]} Nh6 {[%cal Gh6f7]} 3. Bxh6 gxh6 4. Qxf7# 1-0
examples.text:
This example teaches a special trick, clearance.
The white bishop can almost see f7, but a white pawn is blocking its view.
White needs to make room before he can checkmate on f7.
He pushes the pawn, clearing the bishop’s diagonal.

Since the white pawn is now attacking the black bishop, Black moves this bishop out of the way. Now, White’s queen can move to the square that the pawn has left.
The bishop and the queen are now both pointed at the mating square f7.

Black decides to defend by moving his knight to the edge. As we have seen in the previous example, this gets him into trouble.
White removes the knight by taking it with his bishop.
If Black takes back, it is checkmate.
Click on the play button to watch the moves.
